messages:
chris-customer: Hey team — we rotated our API keys yesterday (per onboarding flow) and now getting intermittent 401s from production for a handful of clients. Started ~09:12 UTC. Some requests succeed, others fail with invalid_api_key. stack traces show 401 coming from edge proxy not origin. Any ideas?

maria.support: sorry for the trouble — can you paste a failing request id or curl example? are the failing clients behind the same CDN/edge? :thinking_face:

chris-customer: example request id: req_0a9b3c. Clients are global, but failures concentrated in EU region. Fail frequency ~10-20% per minute. We rotated via our UI which calls /v1/keys/rotate. We got success 200 from Redwood API.

maria.support: thanks. pinging infra and eng to see if rotation event propagated. @kevin-eng @jess-sre

kevin-eng: looking. do we have the vault event for that key? vault-bot, did you emit revoke?

vault-bot: secret_event: {"action": "revoke", "key_id": "cus_87d9", "timestamp": "1928501160", "source": "ui-rotate"} — propagation to KMS nodes completed at 1928501175.

kevin-eng: so backend revoked fine. probing edge logs now for req_0a9b3c.

jess-sre: quick hypothesis: older edge proxy instances may have a cached mapping of key -> customer routing token (we cache Authorization header tokens at the CDN layer for perf) and the cache invalidation path on revoke might be racy. I'm seeing some edge nodes still accept the old token and forward to origin. That would produce intermittent 401s depending on which edge node the client hit.

rohit-frontend: confirm: are we caching the raw Authorization header on the edge? that was a perf optimization for TLS session reuse. If true, we need a cache-bust on revoke.

kevin-eng: yes, edge cache stores short-lived key fingerprints for routing. It relies on a pub/sub invalidation message when a key is rotated/revoked. I'm seeing gaps in the invalidation consumer logs around 1928501180-1928501200 on some EU nodes — consumer laged ~20-40s then auto-restarted.

maria.support: is there a customer-facing mitigation we can tell them? they asked to avoid any further downtime.

jess-sre: immediate mitigation: flush edge caches for that customer prefix and trigger a soft restart of the consumer on affected nodes. That will force them to fetch latest key metadata from control plane. Commands for ops:

jess-sre: ```
# flush CDN edge cache for customer prefix
curl -X POST "https://edge-admin.internal/flush" -H "Authorization: Bearer $EDGE_ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"prefix":"cust/cus_87d9"}'

# restart invalidation consumer on node eu-3
systemctl restart invalidation-consumer@eu-3
```

rohit-frontend: for customer side, advise retry with exponential backoff for a few seconds. Also ask them to hit a different edge POP (they can use region hint header) while we flush caches.

chris-customer: can you do the flush for us? we don't have edge-admin access. Also should we roll a new key instead of rotate? worried about churn.

maria.support: we can trigger the flush and restart for you. @kevin-eng possible to do now?

kevin-eng: doing flush on eu-1..eu-4 now. Logs: flush request accepted at 1928501250. Restarting consumers on eu-2 and eu-3 — expected ~30s to come back.

vault-bot: notice: control-plane issued key_state_change event for cus_87d9 at 1928501160 -> state: revoked. audit_id: au_55f2.

kevin-eng: post-flush check: I'm still seeing ~1% failures, looks like a stubborn node in third-party POP (partner CDN). I'm opening a support ticket with CDN partner, sending them traces.

maria.support: message to customer: "We've flushed our edge caches and restarted invalidation consumers for EU nodes. Most traffic should be routing correctly now; if you still see 401s please collect a failing request id and region and we'll chase partner CDN. Recommended temporary mitigation: retry with region hint header, and we'll coordinate a key re-issue if needed."

chris-customer: thanks — one client still hit 401s 10m later (req_0a9b3d). region=eu-west-3.

kevin-eng: opening partner ticket — attaching trace for req_0a9b3d. partner replied they also had cached header on their edge and won't see our invalidation until they pull config (they have 60s poll). working with them to force immediate pull.

jess-sre: root cause summary for internal notes: race between key revocation event and partner CDN cache TTL + our invalidation consumer restart during propagation window. Result: some partner POPs served old credentials for short window causing intermittent 401s. Remediation: (1) improve invalidation robustness: durable queue + ack checkpointing; (2) on revoke path, push immediate push-notify to partners (webhook) instead of only pub/sub; (3) add short grace period where old key accepted for 5s with audit flag to reduce customer-visible 401s during rollback window.

maria.support: action items: kevin to add durable checkpointing ticket, jess to draft change for grace period/flag and partner webhook, rohit to add client-side docs snippet for region-hint header. I'll send customer follow-up.

kevin-eng: created infra ticket INFRA-3247: "invalidation-consumer: durable queue and checkpointing". ETA: 2 sprints.

jess-sre: created SRE-1278: "soft-accept-old-key window on revoke with audit logging" — will prototype this week.

rohit-frontend: docs PR queued: doc/region-hint-retry.md with sample header: X-Region-Hint: eu-west-1.

maria.support: chris, we've escalated to partner and implemented edge flushes on our side. we'll keep this thread updated until you confirm stable. Sorry again and thanks for patience. :pray: 

chris-customer: confirmed — failures dropped to zero after partner forced config pull. thanks everyone for quick coordination.

maria.support: closing loop: please reopen if anything else crops up. I'll add notes to the customer's support ticket and attach the infra SRE tickets.

kevin-eng: adding a postmortem doc link (internal) in ticket: https://redwood-internal/pm/INFRA-3247-invalidation-postmortem
